clues.title: Plate: black with black dot, or white with blue bar
text: Argentina uses two types of licence plates: a black one, which will be visible on street view with a **black dot** in the middle, and a white one with a **blue bar** at the top.
NOTE: The black dot can only be found on Argentinian licence plates, while the blue bar can be found in Brazil as well.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Two plate types: black with a black dot in the middle, or white with a blue bar on top. The black dot exists only here, but Brazil also has the blue bar.

differs.how: Has the blue bar but never the black dot

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 black car
text: Argentina has a **black** Google car in Generation 3 coverage.
NOTE: Within South America, only Argentina, Peru and Uruguay have a black Google car.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 3 coverage shows a black car. In South America only Peru and Uruguay also have a black car.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 smallcam, low with big blur
text: Argentina also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front.
NOTE: Peru, Brazil and Argentina are the only South American countries with smallcam.

images.caption: Four views of the same road: panned down, back, front and a good front blur

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. Only Peru, Brazil and one other South American country have it.

clues.title: Pole: round concrete, 3 lines alternating, often doubled
text: Round concrete poles sustaining three electricity lines in an **alternating pattern** are very common in Argentina.
**Doubled up poles** like in the second image is also a good clue for Argentina.
NOTE: Similar doubled concrete poles can occasionally be found throughout [Bolivia](https://goo.gl/maps/9soPnAuBufSD1GmH7).

images.caption: Round concrete poles; the red circle magnifies the top of a pole with alternating insulators

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Round concrete poles with three wires in an alternating pattern are very common. Doubled-up poles are a good clue. Bolivia occasionally has similar doubled concrete poles.

clues.title: Pole: wooden poles, A-frame only here in South America
text: Wooden poles are somewhat common in Argentina, they can be found either with a crossbar or without.
NOTE: Wooden A-frame poles in South America are only found in Argentina.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Wooden poles are fairly common, with or without a crossbar. Wooden A-frame poles in South America exist only here.

clues.title: Chevron: white-and-red
text: Argentina typically uses **white-and-red** chevrons.
NOTE: Argentina is the only American country with these chevrons.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Chevrons are usually white and red. No other American country uses them.

clues.title: Road lines: dashed white, double yellow or mixed
text: Road lines in Argentina are mainly dashed** white**, double** yellow** or a mix in between.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Road lines are mainly dashed white, double yellow, or a mix.

clues.title: Marker: white km post with black strip on top
text: Argentinian kilometre markers are typically white with a **black strip** displaying the road number at the top.

NOTE: The markers on national highways are indicated with RN, while RP indicates a provincial highway. National highways will be labelled white on the map, while provincial highways will be labelled green.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White kilometre markers with a black strip showing the road number at the top. RN means national road (white on the map) and RP provincial (green on the map).

clues.title: Guardrail: yellow and red rectangular reflectors
text: **Yellow and red rectangular reflectors** can often be seen on Argentinian guardrails.

NOTE: Within South America, they can also be found in Uruguay.** **However, Uruguayan guardrails can be differentiated from Argentinian guardrails by the shape of their [support](/images/argentina/argentinauruguay_guardrailsupport.jpg).

images.caption: Guardrail with a small yellow and red rectangular reflector on the rail, marked by the arrow and label

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Guardrails often carry yellow and red rectangular reflectors. Uruguay has them too, but its guardrail supports have a different shape.

clues.title: Landscape: flat, treeless, empty and wide open
text: While Argentina features a plethora of different landscapes, most of the country is relatively flat, mostly treeless, and sparsely populated. In the absence of better clues, you should consider Argentina when you see landscapes like this with a very “wide open”, desolate feel.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most of the country is fairly flat, nearly treeless and thinly populated. With no better clue, a wide open, desolate landscape like this points here.

clues.title: Vehicles: unique taxi designs in several cities
text: These Argentinian cities have unique and recognisable taxis.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._

images.caption: Taxi designs of several Argentine cities, each car linked by line to its city on a map

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Several big cities each have their own recognisable taxi design.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains in the far west
text: Far western Argentina typically features a **mountainous** landscape.
NOTE: It is rare to find mountains in eastern Argentina.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The far west is mountainous. Mountains are rare in the east.

clues.title: Landscape: red soil in the north-east tip
text: **Red soil** is typically found in the Misiones province.
NOTE: Brazil and Argentina can look similar in this region. Make sure to look for other clues first.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Red soil is typical of the far north-east province. Brazil looks similar there, so look for other clues first.

differs.how: Looks similar in this region, check other clues

clues.title: Landscape: sandy soil with low trees and bushes
text: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see **sandy soil** with an **abundance of vegetation**; mainly low trees and bushes.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north, sandy soil covered in low trees and bushes.

clues.title: Landscape: grassland with a few tree plantations
text: **Grassland** with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Grassland with a few separate tree plantations is typical of this area.

clues.title: Landscape: small lakes next to the road
text: **Small lakes** near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Small lakes beside the road show up now and then in the big central-east province.

clues.title: Road: reddish pavement lined with long tussock grass
text: Roads with **reddish pavement **lined with **long **[**Argentine needle-grass**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassella_tenuissima)** **are common in San Luis.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Roads with reddish tarmac lined with long needle-grass are common in one central-west province.

clues.title: Landscape: flat and barren, central south
text: **Flat** and **barren** landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Flat, barren land like this is typical of the central south.

clues.title: Plants: flat grass and few bushes in the far south
text: If you see this kind of vegetation with **flat grass** and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Flat grass with few bushes means you are almost certainly in the far-south island province or the south-east of the next province up.

clues.title: Plants: tree plantations in the north-east
text: The majority of **tree plantations** in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.
NOTE: Uruguay and southern Brazil have them as well. Make sure to look at other clues before guessing.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most tree plantations are in the north-east river province. Uruguay and southern Brazil have them too, so check other clues.

differs.how: Also has tree plantations, check other clues

clues.title: Plants: beech forests in the far south
text: **Beech forests** are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Beech forests are common in the far-south island province.

clues.title: Plants: low-density forests of short fan-leaf palms
text: [Coperinicia alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copernicia_alba), also known as the Caranday Wax Palm,** **have short, **fan-like leaves **that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: These palms (Caranday wax palm) have short fan-like leaves and grow in thin, single-species forests. Most common in the north-east, also in nearby provinces.

clues.title: Plants: compact fan palm with dead-leaf trunk coat
text: [Trithrinax Campestris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trithrinax_campestris), or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves** **with a trunk hidden by a **coat of dead-leaves.**

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A hardy palm with compact fan-like leaves and a trunk hidden by a coat of dead leaves. Native to central hills, spreading to the west and north mountains.

clues.title: Plants: arching feathery palms, leaning, mixed heights
text: The [Butia yatay palm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butia_yatay)** **has arching, [pinnate leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnation) and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A palm with arching, feather-like leaves that often leans and varies in height. Most common in the north-east and one national park in the east.

clues.title: Plants: palm with thin leaves, spear top, smooth trunk
text: The [Totai Palm](https://species.wikimedia.org/wiki/Acrocomia_totai) has **small** **thin leaves** with a visible **spear shaped** top, and a **smooth trunk**. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A palm with small thin leaves, a spear-shaped top and a smooth trunk. Planted for decoration everywhere, but wild mostly in the north-east.

clues.title: Plants: candelabra cactus with golden fuzzy spines
text: [Trichocereus atacamensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucostele_atacamensis), or the **cardón**, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The cardon is a candelabra-shaped cactus with fuzzy golden-brown spines, native to the high mountains of the north-west.

clues.title: Plants: tall tree-like cactus with toothpick spines
text: [Stetsonia coryne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stetsonia_coryne), or the **toothpick cactus**, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A big tree-like cactus with many branches and spines like toothpicks. Found around a spot in the north-west centre and on the northern border area.

clues.title: Plants: wild sunflowers in the north-west
text: **Wild sunflowers** ([Tithonia tubaeformis](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tithonia_tubaeformis)) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Wild sunflowers are often found in the three north-west provinces.

clues.title: Plants: large deciduous tree with twisty branches
text: [Prosopis caldenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prosopis_caldenia), known as the caldén, is a decently **large deciduous tree** with **small leaves** and **sinuous branches**. It is mainly found in La Pampa.
NOTE: This tree can sometimes be confused with other trees such as the [White Carob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prosopis_alba).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A fairly large deciduous tree with small leaves and twisting branches, mostly in the central-south plains. It can be confused with other carob-type trees.

clues.title: Plants: pampas grass with white fluffy flowers
text: Pampas grass ([Cortaderia selloana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortaderia_selloana)) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and **white fluffy flowerheads.**

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pampas grass has long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads. It is typical of the central plains.

clues.title: Crops: sugarcane in the north-west
text: **Sugarcane** plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Sugarcane plantations are most common in the north-west, with hotspots in two nearby provinces.

clues.title: Crops: sorghum with dark red heads
text: Fields of [**sorghum**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorghum) can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, Córdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Sorghum fields, with dark red flowerheads, are most common in the central-east provinces.

clues.title: Crops: corn across the north
text: **Corn fields** can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba and Santiago del Estero.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Corn grows in most of the north, most commonly in the centre and north-centre.

clues.title: Crops: sunflower fields in the south of the north
text: Fields of **sunflowers** are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Sunflower fields are mainly in the south of the northern chaco region, and less often in the central east and south of the centre.

clues.title: Plants: rows of tall thin poplars on flat land
text: Single **rows of poplar trees**, characterised by their thin and tall appearance, are very common around Neuquén. The area is also very flat.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Single rows of thin, tall poplar trees are very common around one Patagonian-edge region, and the area is very flat.

clues.title: Pole: wooden hook poles with alternating insulators
text: Within Argentina, these Latvian style **wooden** hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Wooden poles with hook-shaped insulators, like those in Latvia. Within the country, only in two western provinces.

clues.title: Pole: single insulator on the side
text: In Mendoza, poles with a **single insulator **attached to the side of the pole can be found.

images.caption: Wooden pole with a single side insulator, magnified in the red circle at top left

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In one western wine province, poles have a single insulator attached to the side.

clues.title: Pole: white vertical sticker with digits
text: **White** **vertical pole stickers** with several **digits** can be found in Tucumán.

images.caption: Concrete pole with a white sticker of digits, magnified in the red circle at top left

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White vertical pole stickers with several digits are found in one north-west province.

clues.title: Marker: unique markers on provincial roads
text: You can find these unique markers on **provincial roads** in Cordoba.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Distinctive markers appear on the provincial roads of one central province.

clues.title: Sign: yellow junction sign with chevrons at bottom
text: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these **yellow rectangular signs**, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

images.caption: A yellow junction sign with chevrons at the bottom

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: At T-junctions in one central-south province, a yellow rectangular sign with a chevron pattern at the bottom, road numbers above and an arrow on each side.

clues.title: Houses: red bricks in the north-west, like Bolivia
text: **Red bricks**, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Red bricks, like the common ones in Bolivia, appear in the north-west, especially the far west of the northern province.

clues.title: Houses: quartzite facades, orange tiles, vault porches
text: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include **quartzite** **stoned facades**,** orange tiled roofs**, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In a coastal resort city and nearby towns: houses with quartzite stone facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages and vault-shaped porches.

clues.title: Landscape: salt flats in the far north-west
text: **Salt pans** in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.
NOTE: They can also be found in southwestern Bolivia and northeastern Chile.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Salt pans are typically in the far north-west province. They also appear in south-west Bolivia and north-east Chile.

clues.title: Landscape: red mountains along a valley road
text: These **red mountains** are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: These red mountains are unique to the valley of the RN68 road in the south of a north-west province.

clues.title: Landscape: volcanic rocks in Gen 4, high plateau
text: These **volcanic rocks** in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: These volcanic rocks in Gen 4 coverage appear only on RP43 south of a high-altitude village in the north-west.

clues.title: Road: winding dirt road up in the clouds
text: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this **bendy unpaved road up in the mountains** with its western part [up in the clouds](https://maps.app.goo.gl/dq1L8WT13w2QBXpu5).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The western part of RN65 in the north-west is a bendy unpaved mountain road, with its west end up in the clouds.

clues.title: Landscape: red soil, barren, mountain ranges
text: Red soil** **with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in **Parque Nacional Talampaya** in western La Rioja.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Red soil, barren land and mountain ranges, often seen on RN76 in a national park in the west.

clues.title: Landscape: lower hills west of a central city
text: These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.
NOTE: They are not as high as the mountains in the west.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: These mountains are typical west of a central city. They are not as high as the mountains along the western border.

clues.title: Coverage: horse-mounted camera in the south-west
text: This **horse trekker** can be found in southwestern San Juan.
NOTE: A similar trekker can be found on the other side in Chile.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A camera carried on a horse is found in the south-west of a western province. A similar one exists on the Chilean side.

clues.title: Landscape: vineyards, mountains west, flat east
text: If you see** vineyards **with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.
NOTE: There are multiple wine regions in Argentina, but the Mendoza wine region is the most recognisable one of them all.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Vineyards with mountains to the west and flat land to the east mean you are likely in the outskirts of the best-known wine region.

clues.title: Landscape: grassy hills near the coast
text: **Semi-coastal grass hills** are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Grassy semi-coastal hills in the south of the big central-east province, especially north-east of its southern port.

clues.title: Plants: monkey puzzle trees in the west
text: The **monkey puzzle** **tree** can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.
NOTE: They are seen on the other side in Chile** **as well.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Monkey puzzle trees grow in the west of a Patagonian province, with the most along road 23. They also grow on the Chilean side.

clues.title: Google car: black back covered in sandy dust
text: The** “sawdust” **car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The sawdust car is in the central south and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

clues.title: Landscape: rock formations around a dam town
text: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these **rock formations**.
NOTE: Sometimes you will be able to see this [dam](https://goo.gl/maps/C6e9Fto8HjVheSZp7) in the west.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A village in the north-east of a Patagonian province is surrounded by rock formations. Sometimes a dam is visible to the west.

clues.title: Landscape: city built on hill slopes
text: **Comodoro Rivadavia** is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A coastal city is built on the slopes of a hill, which makes it recognisable.

clues.title: Coverage: melting snow near the western border
text: **Melting snow coverage** is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Melting snow coverage appears on the eastern part of RN293 near the Chilean border in the far south-west.

clues.title: Landscape: snowy mountains to the north of a southern city
text: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in **Ushuaia**.
NOTE: Ushuaia is the southernmost city of Argentina and the province capital of Tierra del Fuego.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Snowy mountains lie to the north of the southernmost city, the island province capital. They are found only there.

clues.title: Marker: black-and-white highway markers
text: If you see black-and-white highway markers, you're in Argentina.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Black-and-white highway markers are a good sign you are in this country.

clues.title: Pole: double round concrete poles joined by a ring
text: This double-rounded concrete pole connected by a concrete ring is almost exclusive to Argentina. Similar ones can occasionally be found in Bolivia, but the landscape will be vastly different.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Two round concrete poles connected by a concrete ring are almost exclusive to this country. Bolivia has similar ones only occasionally, with very different scenery.

differs.how: Only occasionally, with very different scenery

clues.title: Landscape: flat, empty land with black car back
text: If you find yourself in a flat, desolate, treeless, sparsely populated area with a visible black back of the Google car, you're likely in Argentina.
(Jordan might resemble this landscape for new players, and it also has a black back on the car, so be aware of that.)
(Only other countries in South America with car like that are: Peru and Uruguay)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A flat, desolate, treeless, thinly populated area with the black back of the Google car points here. Jordan can look similar and also has a black car back.

differs.how: Similar landscape and black car, but different other clues

clues.title: Coverage: thick mist on a mountain road
text: On the 65 in Tucuman, leading west to the Catamarca border near Parque Nacional Aconquija, the Google car drove through what appears to be mist thick enough to clog your windpipe.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On route 65 in the north-west, heading west, the car drives through mist so thick it blocks the view.

clues.title: Coverage: glitchy colours from an early start
text: In the North of Neuquén, the Google driver started their day early and the camera did not like it. As the day progresses, the car goes further north and the glitchy colors fade, until only a bit of color noise remains, and finally, around the province border, it starts to look like normal footage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In the north of a Patagonian province, the camera produced glitchy colours at sunrise. They fade going north and look normal by the province border.

clues.title: Vehicles: black taxi with yellow roof top only
text: Taxis in Jujuy have a **black body** and a **yellow roof**. Notably, only the top of the roof is yellow, making it distinct from Rosario or Buenos Aires taxis.

images.caption: Black taxi with a yellow roof panel

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A taxi with a black body and only the top of the roof yellow. Rosario and the capital have different taxis.

clues.title: Vehicles: red taxi with black stripe
text: **Red taxis** with a **black stripe** are unique to Salta.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Red taxis with a black stripe are unique to one north-west city.

clues.title: Vehicles: all green or all yellow taxi with oval
text: These **all green** or **all yellow** taxis with an oval shape beneath the driver door are unique to Cordoba.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: All-green or all-yellow taxis with an oval shape under the driver's door are unique to one central city.

clues.title: Vehicles: white taxi with yellow roof
text: **White taxis** with a **yellow roof** are unique to San Juan.

images.caption: White taxi with a yellow roof

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: White taxis with a yellow roof are unique to one western province.

clues.title: Vehicles: black and yellow taxi, body only partly black
text: This **black and yellow** taxi is unique to Mendoza. Jujuy, Rosario and Buenos Aires also have black and yellow taxis, but on those taxis, the body is completely black.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: This black and yellow taxi is unique to one wine province. Other cities have black-and-yellow taxis, but with a completely black body.

clues.title: Vehicles: white taxi with blue roof and logo
text: This taxi with the **white body**, **blue roof** and **blue logo** is unique to the city of Bariloche.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A taxi with a white body, blue roof and blue logo is unique to one Andean lake city.

clues.title: Vehicles: old white taxi, yellow-black checker stripe

clues.title: Plants: single-row poplars, hills, vineyards, olives
text: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Tall thin poplars grow all over, but single rows with hilly Mediterranean scenery, vineyards, olives, palms and plane trees mean a town in the two western wine provinces.

clues.title: Plants: light-green cushion plants in Patagonia
text: Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia. It's appearence depends on season.
You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:
Southern Neuquen
Rio Negro on the roads Chasico-Laguna Blanca and Chasico-Ingeniero Jacobacci
Chubut in the area between Paso del Sapo and Gobernador Costa
Also Chubut on the National 40, south of Rio Mayo, as well as the provincial 55 branching east of the 40.

images.caption: Light-green cushion plants on stony Patagonian ground, circled in red.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Cushion-like plants that are found all across Patagonia. In a distinctive light green they appear in the south of one province, on certain roads in the next province, and in the middle and south of the next one.

clues.title: Plants: single-row poplars on very flat land
text: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:
National 22 between Neuquen and Choele Choel (Rio Negro)
Trelew (Chubut)
Sarmiento (Chubut)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Single rows of poplars with a very flat landscape point to certain places: route 22 between two river-valley towns, and two towns in the south-east Patagonian province.

clues.title: Plants: dense, very red grass in the far south
text: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.
In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:
Max South Santa Cruz, latitudes south of Rio Gallegos
The national 40 north of Las Horquetas (Santa Cruz)
The national 40 between Esquel and Estanzia Nueva Lubecka

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A grass with a very red hue. In dense stands it appears at the far southern end south of the southernmost mainland city, on route 40 in the far south, and on route 40 in the south-west.
